text:
ops-bot: PAGER: gpu-pool-exhaustion detected in prod-eu-west1. Inference queue growth on /v1/generate. Autoscaler failing to attach new GPU nodes. Current alert: queue length spike > 10k reqs, tail latency > 2s for 12% of requests. Paging on-call.
Maria B.: seeing a lot of pods Pending with reason=InsufficientGPUs and nodeAffinity/taint mismatch. example:
Maria B.: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | head
inference-req-abc123   0/1     Pending   0          3m    <none>   <none>
```
Maria B.: and node describe shows taint: `redwood.com/gpu-profile=high:NoSchedule` but launchtemplate uses `gpu-profile=standard` for new nodes.
oncall-sre: acked. i'm on it, paging infra lead @AJ. Can you check ASG/launch template versions? :eyes:
AJ: digging in. AWS shows new launch-config/version 5 deployed last night but cluster-autoscaler expects LT v3. ASG max size already at 100, but new nodes failing to register due to LaunchTemplate mismatch + instance profile missing iam:PassRole capability. Error from autoscaler logs:
AJ: ```
E0402 02:01:12.345678 1 scale_up.go:620] failed to create node: LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch: Launch template version 5 not compatible with nodegroup tags
status code: 400, request id: x-yyy
```
Samir M.: also seeing kubelet logs from failed instances: `NodeRegistration: taints applied do not match expected` — looks like cloud-init picks profile `standard-gpu` image which doesn't have the node label agent that adds `redwood.com/gpu-profile=high` taint.
Leila: customer impact: ~120 active customers showing elevated latencies on hosted inference endpoints, worst for long-context models. Rate of 429s up 2x. Ramp started ~02:00UTC.
oncall-sre: mitigation plan:
 1) temp scale up fallback: create emergency nodegroup with manually-correct launch template (LT v3-compatible) and instance profile with iam:PassRole. I can kick that, need @AJ to create LT copy.
 2) cluster-autoscaler fallback: set `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` and `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false`? (we should be conservative) — Samir, advise flags.
Samir M.: I recommend: set `--expander=random` temporarily and `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` not ideal but will allow CA to pick the emergency group. Also set `--nodes=1:200:<emergency-nodegroup-name>` to let CA scale it. Will push patch to CA configmap.
AJ: creating LT clone now with correct userdata that applies `redwood.com/gpu-profile=high` and the proper instance profile. Running:
AJ: ```bash
aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name redwood-emergency-gpu-lt --version-description "emergency-374829" --launch-template-data file://lt-data.json
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name emergency-gpu-asg --launch-template LaunchTemplateName=redwood-emergency-gpu-lt,Version=1 --min-size 0 --max-size 50 --desired-capacity 0
```
AJ: created LT and ASG, pointing CA to group name. requesting oncall-sre to bump desired to 10 to soak.
oncall-sre: bumping desired to 10 now. 10 instances requested.
oncall-sre: nodes are coming up, kubelet registering. first 3 nodes Ready after cloud-init fixes. :white_check_mark:
Maria B.: patching a quick k8s mutating webhook? we need to ensure new nodes get the taint applied if cloud-init misses. Temporary workaround: add DaemonSet that runs `kubectl taint node` on join - but requires RBAC. Might be faster to fix launch template.
Samir M.: I can push a short-lived DaemonSet that watches for nodes without the taint and applies it (iam role already present on nodes). will roll now.
Leila: monitoring metrics: queue length dropped from 10k -> 1.8k in 6 minutes after nodes started. Tail latency back to baseline for 85% of customers. Still ~3% heavy tail, probably older queued requests.
oncall-sre: CA config patched per Samir. Also temporarily increased ASG max for existing gpu pools from 100->140 to give buffer while we stabilize.
AJ: rolling patch to fleet LT to align tags/taints; will coordinate canary: 5% of new nodes for 15m then roll.
oncall-sre: customer impact update to SRE-runbooks and incident page: posting note that inference degradation affected production EU region, mitigation initiated, customers will be contacted if SLA thresholds breached. @Leila please prepare a short blurb for status page.
Leila: drafting status message: "We are experiencing degraded inference performance in EU region due to GPU node provisioning issues. Mitigation in progress; we expect partial recovery within 30 minutes."
Maria B.: follow-ups: need postmortem items: - reconcile LT version drift process - add CI check to verify LT/userdata matches cluster taint expectations - add extra observability for CA scale failures (bubble up AWS error reasons)
Samir M.: root cause hypothesis: automated LT rollout last night inadvertently removed the custom userdata that applies GPU taint/labels and the instance profile change removed PassRole permission; CA attempted to scale but failed due to 400 from AWS and nodes that did come up didn't match taint label so pods stayed Pending.
oncall-sre: status update at +10m: queue length now 600, 99% of customers within SLA, still keeping emergency group alive until LT rollforward is complete. will hand off to next oncall at 02:30UTC.
AJ: leaving ASG + LT changes in place, creating PR for rollback guard and tagging CI to prevent silent LT changes. ping me for ownership on deployment pipeline.
ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: mitigation complete enough for partial closure — emergency group at 10 nodes kept for 1h, CA config reverted to previous safe flags after rampdown. Postmortem assigned to Maria B., AJ, Samir M. Handoff to oncall: @oncall-sre will monitor for 1hr then close.
oncall-sre: handing off to night-shift at 02:30UTC — leaving followup checklist in incident doc. :white_check_mark:
